channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: AI Agents Can Transmit Malicious Commands, Gaining Access to Data
item.description: Cybercriminals can exploit trust between AI agents to spread harmful instructions, potentially leading systems to access restricted services. An independent security researcher highlighted this risk, noting that an attack could begin with a hidden malicious instruction within a document. If connected tools are poorly secured, this could grant access to internal company data.

item.title: Avaza Summit: Central Asian Leaders Prioritize East-West and North-South Transport Corridors
item.description: Leaders from five Central Asian states and Azerbaijan met in Avaza, Turkmenistan, to enhance economic and political cooperation. The summit, hosted by President Serdar Berdimuhamedov, identified East-West and North-South transport corridors as key priorities for regional development. The leaders also proposed increased industrial cooperation and cross-border investment to leverage geographic advantages.

item.title: Trump and Putin Agree on Russian Oil Product Supplies to US and Global Markets
item.description: US President Donald Trump announced an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin for Russia to supply significant quantities of diesel fuel to the US and global markets. Trump stated Russia would immediately deliver over 300,000 tons, with more to follow in November and thereafter. He expects this deal to significantly lower global diesel prices.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Further Cooperation Development with Great Britain
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with UK Minister of State for Trade Lord Anas Sarwar to discuss enhancing mutually beneficial partnerships, particularly in trade and economics. They noted dynamic political dialogue, security cooperation, and growing trade volumes. Several joint ventures and educational partnerships are active.

item.title: Missing Four-Year-Old Boy Found Dead in Construction Site Pit in Kokshetau
item.description: A four-year-old boy, Alan, who went missing on October 8 in Kokshetau, was found dead in a water-filled pit at a construction site. His mother had brought him to work as she had no one to leave him with. Surveillance footage showed him leaving the building and heading towards the construction area. An investigation is underway.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Special Economic Zones Produce 16 Trillion Tenge Worth of Goods
item.description: Kazakhstan operates 18 special economic zones (SEZs), including four established recently. These zones have facilitated 561 investment projects, attracting 11.5 trillion tenge and creating over 38,000 jobs. SEZs produced goods worth 15.9 trillion tenge, with 1.1 trillion tenge exported. Notable projects include a petrochemical complex and a gold refining facility.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan Discuss New Cooperation Prospects in Medicine
item.description: Health ministers from Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan met in Avaza, Turkmenistan, to discuss new cooperation prospects in medicine and pharmaceuticals. They highlighted the growing relations between the two countries in these fields and reviewed initiatives to enhance bilateral partnership, including training programs for doctors and improving primary healthcare.

item.title: Uzbekistan Highlights Priorities for Non-Aligned Movement Parliamentary Network
item.description: Uzbekistan participated in a coordination meeting of the Non-Aligned Movement Parliamentary Network in Tanzania, discussing inter-parliamentary cooperation and coordinating positions for the upcoming IPU presidential election. Uzbekistan, set to chair the network from 2027-2029, emphasized legislative exchange, social protection, women's empowerment, and youth support.

item.title: Uzbek President Awarded FAO's Highest Agricola Medal for Food Security Efforts
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev received the FAO's highest Agricola medal, recognizing his political will and practical actions in ensuring food security, combating hunger and poverty, and developing rural areas. The medal, established in 1977, honors outstanding leaders for their contributions to these critical issues. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN works to ensure sustainable access to quality food for all.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Draft Budget Projects 5.4% GDP Growth and Inflation Down to 6%
item.description: The draft budget for 2027-2029, to be considered by the Kurultai, projects an average annual GDP growth of 5.4% and inflation reduction to 6% by 2029. The budget aims for macroeconomic stability, social obligations fulfillment, and infrastructure development. It also proposes new state awards in arts.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Georgia to Cooperate in Natural Juice Production
item.description: Uzbekistan and Georgia will collaborate on natural juice production, focusing on processing fruits and berries. A meeting between Uzbekistan's Minister of Investment, Industry, and Trade Laziz Kudratov and Georgia's Natural CEO Vladimir Gugushvili discussed attracting foreign investment and utilizing agricultural potential for value-added products.

item.title: President of Turkmenistan Meets with President of the Islamic Republic of Iran
item.description: President Serdar Berdimuhamedow met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who arrived in Turkmenistan for the "Awaza" international coastal forum. Berdimuhamedow expressed gratitude for the invitation and Pezeshkian highlighted the forum's importance for cooperation. They also discussed Turkmenistan's upcoming chairmanship of the CIS in 2026.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Payment Balance Achieves Surplus as Exports Rise and Imports Fall
item.description: Kazakhstan's current account has registered a surplus for the first time in three years, reaching $2.4 billion (1.6% of GDP) in the first half of 2026. This positive shift is attributed to export growth outpacing imports, with non-resource exports showing significant increases, according to the National Bank.

item.title: Turkmenistan President Signs Decrees on Healthcare Reforms
item.description: The President of Turkmenistan signed decrees to establish a new 80-bed Stomatology Center and an International Oncology Science and Clinical Center with 500 beds. These initiatives aim to improve dental and oncological care according to international standards and strengthen the healthcare system's infrastructure.

item.title: President of Turkmenistan Addresses Caspian Ecological Summit
item.description: President Serdar Berdimuhamedow welcomed leaders to the Caspian Ecological Summit, emphasizing the importance of addressing the region's ecological issues at the highest state level. He highlighted the need for continuous, comprehensive efforts to restore the Caspian Sea's environment and biodiversity, advocating for cooperation among Caspian states.

item.title: Over 8,800 Individuals Held Accountable for Public Intoxication in Abai Region
item.description: In the Abai Region, 8,858 individuals have been held accountable for drinking alcohol in public places. Police have intensified checks and patrols to prevent domestic violence and other offenses, with a focus on domestic disputes arising from excessive alcohol consumption. Special measures include restrictions on alcohol consumption for 455 individuals and mandatory treatment for 314 others.

item.title: Caspian Ecological Summit Held in Awaza with Heads of State Present
item.description: A Caspian Ecological Summit convened in the Awaza national tourist zone, chaired by Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedow. Attendees included the presidents of Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan, and Russia. Turkmenistan highlighted its initiatives for developing regional economic and humanitarian ties, emphasizing the importance of the Caspian Sea's ecological well-being for sustainable development.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Build AI-Driven Economy and Industry
item.description: Kazakhstan seeks to leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a driver for economic growth, extending beyond digital tools to impact education, manufacturing, energy, and infrastructure. The goal is to integrate AI into daily work and decision-making processes, transforming the economy. This vision was a key theme at the 'AI & Digital Bridge' forum in Astana.

item.title: Kazakhstan's SEZs Attract 11.5 Trillion Tenge in Investments, Ministry Reports
item.description: Special economic zones (SEZs) in Kazakhstan have attracted 11.5 trillion tenge in investments and implemented 561 projects, creating over 38,000 jobs. The zones produced 15.9 trillion tenge worth of goods, with 1.1 trillion tenge in exports. The Ministry of Industry and Construction highlighted major projects like a gas chemical complex and a precious metals refinery.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Nearly 200 Billion Tenge Saved Through State Procurement Price Comparisons
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Finance reports that using a price database for state planning has saved approximately 200 billion Tenge. Vice Minister Asset Tursunov stated that the system compares prices from various sources, including online marketplaces, to calculate average values. This initiative aims to increase transparency in goods turnover and is part of broader digitalization efforts in public finance.

item.title: Central Asian Rights Group Urges Uzbekistan to Ensure Justice for Ex-Political Prisoners
item.description: The Association 'Human Rights in Central Asia' called on Uzbekistan to guarantee former political prisoners access to justice. At an OSCE conference, the group's head, Nadezhda Atayeva, stated that many released individuals have not achieved rehabilitation or restoration of rights. She urged Uzbekistan to ensure independent case reviews, rehabilitation, and an end to persecution of activists.

item.title: International Criminal Court Condemns US Sanctions as Attack on Rule of Law
item.description: The International Criminal Court has labeled US sanctions against it as an "attack on the rule of law and the foundations of international legal order." The court stated that these sanctions target an independent judicial body established by treaty and mandated by 125 countries to investigate and prosecute genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and the crime of aggression. The ICC asserted that the sanctions aim to disrupt its activities and intimidate its personnel but vowed not to retreat.

item.title: Online Casino Operators in Shymkent Sentenced to Four Years, Assets Confiscated
item.description: Two organizers of illegal online casinos "Bingo-37" and "Lotoboom" in Shymkent have been sentenced to four years in prison. The platforms' total turnover reached 3.1 billion tenge. Assets worth over 200 million tenge, including vehicles and land, were confiscated. The Financial Monitoring Agency reported that players were recruited via WhatsApp and used accounts of 14 'drop-people'.

item.title: US President Trump Pledges No Attack on Iran Before US Elections, Oil Prices Dip
item.description: Global oil prices declined following US President Donald Trump's statement about ongoing negotiations with Iran and no plans to resume military strikes before the November 3 midterm elections. Trump described contacts with Tehran as productive but did not confirm specific agreements. Fears of Middle East conflict escalation and energy supply disruptions eased, impacting oil futures.

item.title: US Imposes Sanctions on International Criminal Court Amid Prosecution Disputes
item.description: The US administration has imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), escalating tensions and potentially straining relations with allies. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated the measures aim to prevent the ICC from prosecuting US citizens and restrict its resources. The ICC condemned the sanctions as an "assault on the rule of law" and vowed to continue its work.

item.title: New York Immigration Officer Shoots Car with Father and Son Inside; Suspect Had Criminal Record
item.description: An immigration officer in New York fired shots at a car carrying a father and his 5-year-old son. The US Department of Homeland Security stated the injured man had prior arrests and ties to a criminal group. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani condemned the officer's actions, demanding a halt to such operations in the city.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National University of Sports Model Developed Considering Regional Needs
item.description: Nurasyl Medeu, founder of the Kazakh National University of Sports (KNUS), discussed the institution's unique development. He explained the idea arose from observing a lack of professional sports training in Kazakhstan during his youth. Medeu aimed to integrate the structured sports education system he witnessed in the US to foster talent in Kazakhstan and Central Asia.

item.title: Abai University Hosts Conference on Nomadic Civilization Research
item.description: Abai University held an international scientific-practical conference titled 'Nomadism – A Type of Culture and Civilization: Modern Interpretation.' The event focused on studying the historical and cultural heritage of nomadic civilization, its place in human culture, and reinterpreting traditional values in a contemporary context. The conference also marked the 50th anniversary of a key monograph on nomadic aesthetics.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Use Artificial Intelligence to Assess State Property Efficiency
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to implement artificial intelligence to evaluate the efficient use of state-owned buildings and vehicles. Vice Minister of Finance Asset Tursunov stated that AI will assess how effectively state property is utilized. The Digital Qazyna system already contains data on 25.6 million state property objects owned by 19,000 organizations.

item.title: Uzbekistan and UK Discuss Establishing International Financial Center in Tashkent
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with UK Minister of State for Trade, Anne-Marie Trevelyan. The British side expressed readiness to assist in establishing an International Financial Center in Tashkent, operating on "English law" principles. This initiative aims to bolster financial sector development and international cooperation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Faces Shortage of Donor Organs, 126 Children Await Transplants
item.description: In Kazakhstan, 4,867 individuals are on the organ transplant waiting list, including 126 children. As of September 1, 17,158 consent forms for posthumous donation were registered. The Ministry of Health reported 208 transplants in the first nine months of the year, with 42 from deceased donors. Public fears and myths hinder donation consent.

item.title: Financial Aid Allocated to Families of Soldiers Deceased in Caspian Incident
item.description: A commission has completed its work on allocating financial aid to the families of military personnel who died or were injured during a tragic incident in the Caspian Sea. The "National Spirit" fund, established to collect charitable donations from major enterprises, entrepreneurs, and patrons, has distributed all collected funds. This aid is provided as per President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's directive.

item.title: Central Asian leaders pledge unity but actions lag behind rhetoric on cooperation
item.description: Leaders of six Central Asian nations and Azerbaijan met to discuss closer economic cooperation, trade, transport, and regional security. Turkmenistan expressed readiness to expand trade and digitalize economies, signaling a shift from its isolationist policies. President Berdymukhamedov called for a unified approach to key issues.

item.title: TRIPP project stalled by external factors, hindering Middle Corridor development
item.description: The Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project, intended to connect Azerbaijan to its exclave via Armenia, remains stalled over a year after its agreement. Principal obstacles are external, impeding the broader Middle Corridor initiative connecting Central Asia to Europe. The project aimed to integrate Armenia and Azerbaijan into this vital trade route.

item.title: Kazakhstan Implements Digital Taxpayer Dossiers, Yielding 322 Billion Tenge Effect
item.description: Kazakhstan's Smart Data Finance system has created digital dossiers for taxpayers using data from 80 sources, resulting in an effect of 322 billion tenge. The system helps match income and expenses, and pre-fills tax declarations. As part of the new Tax Code, integrated tax administration changes will be implemented from January 1, 2026, simplifying administration and reducing reporting.

item.title: US State Department Report: Taliban and Other Groups Unlawfully Recruit Child Soldiers in Afghanistan
item.description: The US State Department's 2026 Trafficking in Persons Report states that the Taliban and other armed groups in Afghanistan unlawfully recruit and use children. Groups like ISIS-K and the NRF reportedly use child soldiers in combat and support roles, including planting explosives and guarding bases.

item.title: Desperate Afghans Sell Kidneys to Escape Debt and Hunger
item.description: Facing overwhelming debt and unable to feed their children, desperate Afghans are selling their kidneys on the black market. Zahira, a mother of two, sold one kidney last year, but it did not save her family from poverty and has negatively impacted her health. An estimated number of impoverished Afghans are selling organs, primarily kidneys, to survive amid the worsening humanitarian crisis since the Taliban takeover.

item.title: China tightens vehicle export rules, requiring service centers abroad from 2027
item.description: China will implement stricter vehicle and motorcycle export regulations starting in 2027. Exporters must establish overseas service centers, provide cooperation agreements, repair documentation, and proof of staff qualifications. Rules for re-equipped vehicles are also tightening, requiring official manufacturer approval.

item.title: Erkinjon Turdimov Appointed First Deputy Prime Minister for Education and Science
item.description: Erkinjon Turdimov has been appointed First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Education and Science of Uzbekistan. He was released from his position as governor of Sirdaryo region. The new position was created within the executive structure of the Cabinet of Ministers. Saida Mirziyoyeva will oversee the implementation of tasks in education, science, and healthcare.

item.title: Caspian Summit Agrees to Form Joint Commission on Declining Water Levels
item.description: At the Caspian Ecological Summit in Turkmenistan's Awaza tourist zone, the five littoral states agreed to establish a joint commission to study the causes of the sea's declining water levels and prepare joint measures against its negative impacts. The decision was made by the presidents of Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan, and Russia.
